author: NorthEast News Desk
body: U.S. holiday retail sales are expected to grow faster in 2026, with Deloitte forecasting an increase of as much as 4.8% during the crucial year-end shopping period, Reuters reported Thursday.

Deloitte tied the outlook to growth in disposable income, which could support spending even as households absorb higher fuel and other everyday costs. The forecast suggests consumers will continue searching for value while reserving room for selected discretionary and seasonal purchases.

The projection matters for retailers because the holiday quarter often determines annual performance. Merchants must balance promotions for budget-conscious households with inventory for customers willing to spend more on a smaller number of items. Forecast growth does not guarantee equal gains across chains, product categories or income groups.

The estimate is a forward-looking forecast rather than a report of completed sales. Results will depend on inflation, employment, fuel costs, promotions and the timing of purchases. Retailers and investors will compare the outlook with incoming consumer-spending data and company guidance as the season approaches, while watching whether higher costs change the mix of goods shoppers buy.
dek: The firm forecasts sales could rise as much as 4.8%, supported by disposable income even as shoppers remain focused on value.
headline: Deloitte sees faster U.S. holiday retail-sales growth in 2026
